prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Summary of the 1997 manifesto (within 500 words; ideological framing removed; no party or individual names)

- Constitutional plan and governance
  - Independence route: win a majority of Scottish MPs at a UK general election, negotiate with the UK and EU (6–12 months), hold a single-question referendum on the settlement, then declare independence and hold fresh elections.
  - Post-independence framework: written constitution and Bill of Rights; unicameral parliament elected by proportional representation; voting age 16+; petition-led legislation; entrenched local government with PR; reform of the monarchy’s role; broad civil, social, and economic rights.

- Economy, taxation, and jobs
  - Target full employment; create 100,000 additional jobs and expand apprenticeships.
  - Business taxes: reduce main corporation tax to 30p, small companies’ rate to 18p; abolish Class IV National Insurance for the self-employed; introduce banded business rates favoring smaller firms.
  - Investment: new funds for R&D, exports unit, skills foundation, tourism marketing, transport projects, rural and marine development, sustainable development.
  - Personal taxes: introduce a 15p starter income tax rate; widen the basic-rate band; remove the National Insurance ceiling; cut VAT on domestic fuel to 5%; raise tobacco duty; reduce spirits duty.
  - Debt and budget: assume a population share of UK debt (~£38bn) and repay £6.6bn over four years; reallocate spending from nuclear deterrent to public services. Claims a continuing fiscal surplus relative to the UK.

- Social policy, health, and justice
  - Child benefit increase; restore benefits to 16–17s; pension increases; cold-climate allowance; abolish means testing for residential elderly care; remove utility standing charges for pensioners.
  - Health: abolish the internal market; create national and local health commissions; +£35m annually; reintegrate dentistry; review prescription charges; ban tobacco advertising; strengthen food and consumer health through an independent agency.
  - Justice: support “zero tolerance” community policing; improve prosecutions service; emphasize alternatives to prison and rehabilitation; strengthen drug education, data, and local action teams; ban handguns with compensation and tighter firearms controls.

- Education, housing, local services, culture
  - Hire 700 teachers; repair schools; expand school-level budget control; universal school internet access and more classroom computers.
  - Free nursery education for 3–4s; restore higher-education maintenance grants; expand training and employment grants; support Gaelic-medium education and broader cultural/language inclusion.
  - Housing: transfer 75% of council housing debt to central government in four years; build up to 20,000 affordable homes; upgrade substandard stock; protect new/improved social housing from discounted right-to-buy; create a new housing agency.
  - Local government: restore powers from quangos; reform finance; abolish water quangos. Culture: reform broadcasting with a national public broadcaster plus commercial diversity; film incentives; refocus arts funding; create a Scottish lottery and ban scratch cards.

- Land, rural economy, environment, energy, transport, telecoms
  - Abolish feudal tenure; establish a land commission, all-Scotland land register, and community-focused shoreline/seabed management.
  - Agriculture: rapid traceability; CAP reform; diversification; market access; food standards agency partnership.
  - Forestry: new enterprise board; double woodland cover in 25 years; expand wood industries and access.
  - Crofting: new development agency; enable estate buyouts; return Crown crofting estates to residents under clear rules.
  - Fisheries: regional management councils; processing support; stronger enforcement; technical conservation; more research; targeted funding.
  - Environment: strengthen the regulator; stricter pollution controls; rehabilitation; public consultation; national targets; end nuclear reprocessing at Dounreay; create renewables R&D center.
  - Energy: allocate North Sea assets by existing legal demarcation/equidistance; sustain oil and gas; address gas transmission pricing; consider shared network ownership with a public golden share; reassess coal; phase out nuclear generation; expand renewables and conservation.
  - Transport: invest in rail (including electrification) and bring Scottish Railtrack assets into public ownership; integrate bus/rail; remove Skye Bridge tolls (move to public ownership); support ferries; adjust/abolish air passenger duty for remote areas; enhance air links.
  - Telecoms: stronger regulation of monopolies; rural connectivity; distance learning; promote internet access and industry; no new content controls, but support ratings; update laws on digital fraud.

- Europe, international relations, defence, and aid
  - Full EU membership with voting rights, Commissioner, presidency rotation, more MEPs, and PR for elections; prioritize fisheries and agriculture negotiations and EU structural funds.
  - Targeted diplomatic presence; membership of UN, Council of Europe, Commonwealth; propose an Association of States of the British Isles.
  - Defence: establish national army, navy, and air force using existing bases; prioritize joint training; withdraw nuclear deterrent; phase withdrawal from NATO while maintaining wider cooperation; create a peacekeeping college; promote defence diversification with domestic procurement within EU rules.
  - Overseas aid: raise spending to 0.7% of GDP within six years.
